I have a very interesting case: At slot [15341](https://dora.peerdas-devnet-3.ethpandaops.io/slot/15341), `prysm-geth-2-arm` (Full node) proposed a block. It broadcasted all the data columns, but received 8 invalid data columns, for the same slot, from Nimbus and Lodestar. Logs: https://gist.github.com/nalepae/4a0b9a2c71402235d11ef90150eb7691 i suspect the messages from nimbus has been generated during broadcasting reconstructed columns. but can this cause so many multiple forks? i have been a bit weary about it for a while because if it were from proposed ones, the clients would have complained way earlier Well, even if nimbus broadcasts invalid messages, the rest of the network should be resilient to these messages. (At least rejecting them, and possibly disconnect nimbus peers) exactly Actually I'm wondering if Prysm (which seems to be the only one fully live and fully in one fork client) is not the only client which did not do something correctly. (like accepting invalid stuffs) i think the length mismatch is not checked by some of the clients while checking rpc responses i think the length checks should be independently included as a part of `inclusion proof check` as well, if it is not yet cc <@592004585506340885> or, all clients should verify inclusion proof as well as verify dc sidecar kzg proof in checking responses from rpc that's because if incorrect dcs are reconstructed then they might just be persisted to db as well, and if they are persisted to db as well, they might as well be collected as an rpc response via some other client, and ignored/ not-so-satisfactorily verified this plan might hurt the latency tho Hum interesting. The specification of [by root](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7594/p2p-interface.md#datacolumnsidecarsbyroot-v1) only requests to check `verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs` and not `verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof`. (But Prysm verifies both on `byRoot` RPC response. That *could* explain why Prysm is still alive.) exactly 🙂 well atleast the bug helps refine the spec 🙂 Well I spoke a little bit too fast, the spec exactly tells: > Before consuming the next response chunk, the response reader SHOULD verify the data column sidecar is well-formatted, **has valid inclusion proof**, and is correct w.r.t. the expected KZG commitments through verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs. ==> `has valid inclusion proof` is what we translated in prysm by "run the `verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof` function" In that case the spec is indeed accurate Should the `SHOULD` be replaced by a `MUST`? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3963

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
I have a very interesting case:
At slot [15341](https://dora.peerdas-devnet-3.ethpandaops.io/slot/15341), `prysm-geth-2-arm`  (Full node) proposed a block.
It broadcasted all the data columns, but received 8 invalid data columns, for the same slot, from Nimbus and Lodestar.
Logs: https://gist.github.com/nalepae/4a0b9a2c71402235d11ef90150eb7691

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: i suspect the messages from nimbus has been generated during broadcasting reconstructed columns. but can this cause so many multiple forks?

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: i have been a bit weary about it for a while

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: because if it were from proposed ones, the clients would have complained way earlier

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Well, even if nimbus broadcasts invalid messages, the rest of the network should be resilient to these messages.
(At least rejecting them, and possibly disconnect nimbus peers)

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: exactly

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: Actually I'm wondering if Prysm (which seems to be the only one fully live and fully in one fork client) is not the only client which did not do something correctly.

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: (like accepting invalid stuffs)

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: i think the length mismatch is not checked by some of the clients while checking rpc responses

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: i think the length checks should be independently included as a part of `inclusion proof check` as well, if it is not yet cc <@592004585506340885>

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: or, all clients should verify inclusion proof as well as verify dc sidecar kzg proof in checking responses from rpc

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: that's because if incorrect dcs are reconstructed then they might just be persisted to db as well, and if they are persisted to db as well, they might as well be collected as an rpc response via some other client, and ignored/ not-so-satisfactorily verified

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: this plan might hurt the latency tho

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Hum interesting. The specification of  [by root](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7594/p2p-interface.md#datacolumnsidecarsbyroot-v1) only requests to check `verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs` and not `verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof`.

(But Prysm verifies both on `byRoot` RPC response. That *could* explain why Prysm is still alive.)

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: exactly

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: well atleast the bug helps refine the spec 🙂

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Well I spoke a little bit too fast, the spec exactly tells:
> Before consuming the next response chunk, the response reader SHOULD verify the data column sidecar is well-formatted, **has valid inclusion proof**, and is correct w.r.t. the expected KZG commitments through verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs.

==> `has valid inclusion proof` is what we translated in prysm by "run the `verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof` function"

excerpts.author: agnxsh
excerpts.content: In that case the spec is indeed accurate

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: Should the `SHOULD` be replaced by a `MUST`?
